name: GS23301 VPA-1 Rwanda Clean Cookstoves project
description:
The purpose of the VPA is to distribute Improved cookstoves in households and communities of Rwanda, Africa. The Improved cookstoves are distributed to households/institutions which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for cooking/boiling. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the  burning of large amount of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal in baseline scenario. 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda, Africa where the Improved cookstoves are proposed to be distributed.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: SPOUTS Distributed Technology Devices Program in Rwanda

name: Durable Solutions Congo: Clean energy and environmental resilience in the DRC
description:
The Durable Solutions Congo: Clean energy and environmental resilience in the DRC, is a Programme of Activities (PoA) whose purpose is to improve access to efficient cookstoves and safe water supply technologies for low-income households in  rural and peri-urban areas throughout the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The technologies distributed under this PoA aim to address pressing environmental, health and social challenges in a locally appropriate manner. 
Serving as the starting point, the real-case VPA intends to contribute towards the goals of the PoA by distributing the “Sala Makala Stove,” a Top-Lit Up-Draft (TLUD) stove capable of combusting firewood more efficiently than traditional/3-stone biomass cookstoves. Thereby saving approximately 2.04 tCO2e per household per year. The project further aims to improve air quality and subsequently, household health, by reducing exposure to harmful smoke, as well as reducing fuelwood consumption with greater stove efficiency.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Integrated climate action, adaptation, and CO2 reduction to improve environmental management, livelihoods, and youth empowerment in Inhambane and Gaza Provinces
description: This project will be implemented in the Mozambican provinces of Inhambane and Gaza, reaching local communities that rely on traditional biomass fuels for cooking. Its central strategy is the promotion and deployment of improved charcoal and firewood cookstoves (ICS), aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and generate environmental, social, and economic benefits aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Implementation will be led by TDH Germany (project owner) and MAHLAHLE (local implementer), combining international standards with local knowledge for effective delivery. The project will deploy 9,000 charcoal ICS, all compliant with Gold Standard requirements and locally manufactured or assembled at a dedicated facility. These stoves will increase combustion efficiency, reduce indoor air pollution, cut emissions, and lower household energy costs. Over the first five-year crediting period, the project is expected to reduce 81,000 tons of CO₂e, based on Gold Standard TPDDTEC methodology. Designed to deliver multiple co-benefits, it contributes to SDG13 (climate action through 81,000 tCO₂e reductions), SDG15 (forest conservation), and SDG3 (better health from cleaner air). Socially, it advances SDG3 (reduced smoke exposure), SDG4 (environmental clubs for climate literacy), SDG5 (gender equality through time savings for women), and SDG6 (improved sanitation via water systems). Economically, it supports SDG1 (lower household fuel expenses), SDG7 (cleaner cooking for 9,000 households), and SDG8 (job creation in production, distribution, and education).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Infosys Agroforestry Project for Rural Farmers in India
description: The project seeks to promote agroforestry in rural areas of India. The project's focus is to improve livelihood of the farmer community by enhancing their social and economic status. The project will not only remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere but will also help in building climate resilience among the farming community. The agroforestry system will improve soil fertility, reduce erosion, enhance water retention, and increase resilience to climate shocks such as drought and flooding. The project avoids environmental degradation by reducing synthetic fertilizer dependency and preventing land degradation.

name: Community Safe Water Project in Ethiopia
description:
The project activity includes realization of solar powered safe drinking water systems situated in the Afar, East Hararghe, Somali, Guji and Gumuz regions.
The project is addressed to supply safe drinking water for domestic use and consequently to improve the hygiene, social, economic and environmental issues related to the water cycle in rural areas. Moreover, verifiable Carbon Dioxide (CO2) emission reductions are achieved through the reduced wood combustion and the need for water purification through boiling is reduced. The project will also raise awareness among population regarding hygiene and contribute to sustainable development.

name: Sustainable Rice Production in Southeast and South Asia
description: The Programme of Activities (PoA), titled 'Sustainable Rice Production in South East and South Asia', is a multi-country initiative that promotes the adoption of a suite of sustainable agricultural practices. The project's core measure is Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), a climate-smart irrigation technique aimed at reducing methane emissions and conserving water in rice fields. While initial implementation is focused on rice-growing regions in Indonesia and Vietnam, the project is designed with a long-term vision to scale across other countries in South and Southeast Asia. The primary goal is to generate quantifiable carbon and water benefits, with a broader aim to improve the overall environmental and social sustainability of rice farming by incorporating measures that address soil health, energy efficiency, and pollution control.

name: BIWACALI
description:
BIWACALI stands for Burka Initiative for Water Balancing, Carbon Sequestration and Livelihood Improvement. The Oromo word “Burquaa” means “burbling spring”, symbolizing the main objective of this project: ensuring the water security of the West-Ethiopian Upper Dabana - and the East-Ethiopian Hakim Gara watersheds by restoring about 10,000 ha areas degraded area into forest over the next decades. This will be achieved by tree planting and applying the Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) technique, which is designed to significantly improve the income and livelihoods of local farming communities. 

Next to the physical restoration work, major project activities are the formation of cooperatives and unions for forest management and training on FMNR, sustainable farming methods and alternative livelihoods. The newly created cooperatives will be strongly supported by World Vision Ethiopia in the first years of the project. It is envisioned that afterwards, they will take on the main responsibility for managing the forest areas, their products and the monitoring of the project impacts. 

The project is being implemented jointly by the local communities, Heineken Ethiopia, World Vision Ethiopia and FORLIANCE.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

The project aligns with the Gold Standard's objectives of delivering real, measurable, and long-term emission reductions and promoting sustainable development benefits.

name: GS23401 VPA-1 Sustainable Rice Cultivation for Smallholder Farmers in India
description:
The VPA aims to reduce methane emissions from irrigated paddy fields by implementing the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique. Unlike traditional continuous flooding methods, AWD involves intermittent flooding, allowing fields to dry at certain intervals. This approach significantly reduces methane production while also lowering water consumption, making it both environmentally, socially and economically beneficial.
In addition to promoting AWD, the VPA will support participating farmers with a comprehensive package of best practices tailored to optimize rice cultivation in the region.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23399 VPA-1 Renewable Biomass Briquette Production for Clean Energy
description: The proposed project involves the production and supply of approximately 10,200 tonnes of biomass briquettes annually, with the objective of replacing conventional fossil fuels such as coal, furnace oil, and firewood that are commonly used by industries and institutions for thermal energy applications. The primary goal is to promote the use of clean, renewable, and sustainable biomass energy while reducing reliance on carbon-intensive fuels. These briquettes are manufactured using agricultural residues and other organic biomass waste, which are typically discarded or left to decompose, resulting in methane emissions and environmental degradation. By converting this waste into high-density fuel briquettes, the project addresses key environmental and economic challenges. It contributes to greenhouse gas emission reductions by displacing fossil fuels and preventing methane emissions from un-managed biomass waste. The initiative also supports improved waste management through the productive use of agricultural residues, offers access to cleaner-burning fuels for small and medium-sized industrial units, and generates local employment across the biomass value chain—from raw material collection and processing to transportation and distribution. Additionally,by reducing the use of coal and wood, the project helps improve air quality and public health through lower emissions of particulate matter and other harmful pollutants.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Green Briquettes for Fossil Fuel Displacement in South Africa

name: VPA1-GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India
description:
The proposed project activity is the voluntary action undertaken by Landmark Agri Exports Pvt. Ltd., and WeAct Pty Ltd. The project falls under the Agriculture category introducing improved agricultural practices in rice cultivation.

This project aims to reduce methane (CH4) emissions through improved water management practices involving alternate wetting and drying (AWD) of the paddy lands. AWD is a proven method to reduce CH4 emission by as much as 48% compared to continuously flooded conditions where high rates of CH4 are emitted by the lands due to the anaerobic decomposition of the organic matter . Rice is the most prominent food crop in India. It is the backbone of livelihood for millions of rural households and plays a vital role in the country’s food security. India is one of the world's largest producers and exporters of rice and hence plays an important part in the country’s economy. The proposed VPA activity is planned to be implemented in the Madhya Pradesh State of India.

This VPA is implemented in Seoni district covering 26,103 ha in 8 tahsils
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India
description: This is a Programme of Activities (PoA) called “GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India” in India that will include various Voluntary Project Activities (VPAs) in it. The “GS PoA for Sustainable Rice Cultivation Projects in India” consists of implementation of Alternate and Wetting and Drying (AWD) practice in India. Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method and aerobic rice cultivation method is a scientifically proven way of managing rice fields for better water management and achieving reduction or avoidance of methane emissions that is caused in traditional submerged rice fields. Therefore, Landmark Agri Exports Pvt. Ltd. (an Indian entity) & WeAct Pty Ltd. (an Australian entity) has taken a voluntary initiative to develop a project in India that is designed specifically for Rice fields to adopt AWD and other adjusted water managements methods, to be implemented across various states of India. Thus, the main objective of the project is to avoid flooded irrigation in rice fields and adopt AWD/other adjusted water management methods for rice cultivation to reduce methane emissions from the rice fields.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
